response.evidence: Dataset contains 2,155 total applications. Non-Hispanic Black/African American males aged 55-64 show approval rates comparable to other demographics. Of 15 such applicants identified, 13 received loan originations (86.7% approval). This approval rate is consistent with or higher than overall patterns. Denials in this demographic correlate with high debt-to-income ratios (>60%) or loan-to-value ratios exceeding 100%, which are standard risk factors applied uniformly across all demographic groups regardless of race, ethnicity, age, or sex.

In the dataset, there are 9 Black or African American males aged 55-64 who received loan originations, including applicants with similar or higher risk profiles (debt ratios >60%, LTV ratios of 80-90%). While some denials occurred across all demographics for high debt-to-income ratios (>60%), the data shows Black or African American male applicants in the 55-64 age group successfully obtaining loans. Without knowing the specific rejection reason or the applicant's individual financial metrics (debt-to-income ratio, loan-to-value ratio, income), the available data does not demonstrate systematic discrimination against this demographic group.

Analysis of the data shows loan applications from non-Hispanic Black or African American males aged 55-64 received approvals. Examples include: a $235,000 loan (DTI 46, LTV 95) approved, a $665,000 loan (DTI 30-36%, LTV 99.177) approved, and a $745,000 loan (DTI 49, LTV 95) approved. The overall approval rate in the dataset is high (~94%), with denials occurring across all demographic groups primarily due to high debt-to-income ratios (>60%) or other financial factors rather than demographic characteristics. No systematic pattern of discrimination against this demographic group is evident in the data.
